tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: As per our disclosure dated February 28, 2025, the Company had informed that assessing officer had issued an order with demand of Rs 64.22 crore on 27.02.2025.The Company filed an appeal against the said order before CIT(Appeals). CIT(A) issued order against the Company without providing adequate opportunity of being heard Crisil Limited filed an appeal before ITAT on October 16, 2025
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Crisil Limited has filed an appeal before ITAT against CIT(A) order
tax_litigation.status: ITAT has issued favourable order and remanded back to CIT(A) for fresh adjudication.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company had received demand order on 31/12/2025 for alleged disagreement regarding admissibility of credit notes in FY 2018-19. The Company made LODR disclosure on 01/01/2026.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The Assistant Commissioner, CGST & Central Excise, Div- VIII, Mumbai East, Commissionerate
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed appeal against the order on 26/03/2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: As per our last disclosure dated March 24, 2026, the Assessing Officer had issued a reassessment order for AY 2017–18 pertaining to the Company's merged subsidiaries. The AO erroneously computed the tax by making unwarranted additions and failing to give credit for taxes already paid, which resulted in an incorrect demand order and raised a demand of Rs. 121.20 crore. The Company was in the process of filing an appeal against the order before the CIT(Appeals).
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal before CIT(A) on April 21, 2026

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: As per our last disclosure dated March 30, 2026, the Assessing Officer had issued order for TDS demand (including interest) of Rs. 27.23 crore with respect to foreign payments. The demand was raised based on previous years’ orders on the same issue against which the company has filed an appeal before Hon’ble CIT(Appeals). The Company was in the processing of filing an appeal against the said order before the CIT (Appeals).
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal before CIT(A) on April 27, 2026

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: As per our last disclosure dated April 21, 2026, the Assessing Officer had passed an order under Section 143(3) read with Section 144B of the Income-tax Act, for AY 2023-24 with certain disallowances and raising a Tax demand (including interest) of Rs. 148.99 crore. The Company was in the processing of filing an appeal against the said order before the CIT (Appeals).
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal before CIT(A) on May 20, 2026

operating_notes.text: Corporate bond issuance fell 18% in H1 2026 to ₹5,456 billion and 26% in Q2 2026 to ₹2,693 billion, while bank credit growth was 19.2% in Q2 2026.
Ratings segment margin rose to 44.3% in Q2 2026 from 41.0% in Q2 2025; Research, Analytics & Solutions margin was 20.4% against 20.0%.

timeline.summary: Minal Bhosale, ACS, recorded the Analyst Call held on April 20, 2026, for NSE and BSE compliance.
Crisil received income tax assessment order with ₹148.99 Cr demand for AY 2023-24 on April 21, 2026
Crisil held its analyst conference call on April 20, 2026, discussing Q1 CY26 financial performance and business updates.
Crisil Limited’s **Amit Bhosale** and **Minal Bhosale** scheduled a virtual analyst meet with Goldman Sachs on June 4, 2026, using the latest corporate presentation.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,095.16 Cr (+20.2% YoY), net profit ₹204.54 Cr (+5.9% YoY).
Crisil published its investor presentation updated with Q3 2026 financial results on October 23, 2026.
